matchstick.title: Compute numeric discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compute the left‑hand side and right‑hand side. This reveals how far the current equation is from being true and guides which part needs adjustment.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a matchstick equation, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: IX = XII + IV → 9 vs 16, discrepancy of 7.

matchstick.title: Enumerate single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: List all Roman‑numeral characters that can be obtained by adding or removing a single matchstick from each character in the equation. This defines the complete set of possible one‑stick changes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning which stick to move, generate all one‑stick variations of each numeral and operator.
matchstick.example: I can become II by adding a vertical stick; V can become X by repositioning a diagonal.

matchstick.title: Validate source and destination characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, ensure that the character you removed it from still forms a valid Roman numeral or operator, and that the character you added it to also becomes a valid one.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick relocation, before accepting the move.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' leaves '-', which is valid; adding it to 'XII' creates an extra I, forming 'XIII'.

matchstick.title: V↔X transformation (reposition diagonal)
matchstick.principle: A diagonal stick from a V can be repositioned to cross the other diagonal, turning V (5) into X (10); moving a diagonal away from an X can create a V, changing the value by ±5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy suggests a change of 5 and a V or X is present in the equation.
matchstick.example: Changing V to X adds 5 to the numeral.

matchstick.title: I↔II vertical addition/removal
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to an I creates a second I (II), increasing the value by 1; removing a vertical stick from II reduces it to I, decreasing the value by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy is ±1 and an I or II appears in the equation.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to 'XII' yields 'XIII'.

matchstick.title: Operator change – to + (or + to –)
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical turns it into a minus sign, while adding a vertical to a minus creates a plus. This switches addition to subtraction or vice versa.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is close but the operator needs to be switched to balance the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Turning '+' into '-' while moving its vertical stick to another numeral.

matchstick.title: Never alter the equality sign
matchstick.principle: The '=' sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; moving any stick away or adding to it destroys the equality and makes the equation invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Throughout the solving process; never consider moving sticks from or to the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Do not take a horizontal stick from '=' to change a numeral.

matchstick.title: Respect stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Sticks retain their orientation; a diagonal stick cannot be used as a vertical or horizontal stick, and vice versa. The target character must accept the stick’s orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When repositioning a stick, verify that its orientation matches the requirements of the destination character.
matchstick.example: A diagonal from V cannot become the vertical of I.

matchstick.title: Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick relocation, recompute the integer values of the entire equation to verify that it now holds. This catches moves that look plausible visually but are numerically wrong.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any proposed move, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: After moving the vertical from '+' to 'XII', recalculate: IX = XIII - IV → 9 = 13 - 4 → 9 = 9.

matchstick.title: Plus‑to‑minus vertical transfer for numeral increment
matchstick.principle: If the equation is off by exactly one and a plus sign is present, you can move the vertical stick from the plus sign to the numeral that needs to increase, simultaneously turning '+' into '-' and adding an I to the numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy is ±1 and the operator is '+', consider moving its vertical stick to create an extra I in a numeral.
matchstick.example: IX = XII + IV → move vertical from '+' to the right of the two I's in XII, yielding IX = XIII - IV.

matchstick.description: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical I
matchstick.why_it_happens: Model confuses stick orientation and assumes any stick can represent I.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check the orientation of each stick; only vertical sticks can form I.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Model tries to move sticks from '=' to adjust values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never consider moving sticks from or to the '=' sign.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid source character after removal
matchstick.why_it_happens: Model removes a stick without ensuring the remaining shape matches a valid numeral/operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Validate the source character after removal.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Model overlooks that a plus can become minus by moving a vertical stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Consider operator change as a possible single‑stick move.

matchstick.description: Skipping arithmetic verification after a visual change
matchstick.why_it_happens: Model assumes the visual change fixes the equation without recomputing values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑evaluate the numeric equality after each move.
